rounds.deathAnalysis: You played aggressive without utility on the opening, and you keep taking deaths like this in early rounds; as Brimstone, don't step into a wide angle on entry without a molly or smoke — smoke first and wait for your team.
enemyAnalysis: This is a pistol-economy round; even without full rifles, the enemies are dangerous at close range.
As Brimstone, set up two smoke lines next round — throw one on the entry and save the other for a retake or to cut the side angle.
rounds.nextRoundSuggestion: On defense this is a pistol round, so don't swing wide alone toward A or B; close the entry choke with a smoke, save the molly to delay the plant or defuse, and move in with your team.

rounds.deathAnalysis: You were left in the open and the enemy shot you from an angle — on defense you didn't sit on the edge with a tight off-angle, so you died to a one-shot angle; as Brimstone, move to the edge and don't leave that corner open without cutting vision with a smoke.
enemyAnalysis: The enemy roster has Chamber, and he held the long sightline; he took you out in one shot from range.
From now on, close that angle with a smoke and keep a teammate next to you so a single angle can't pick you off quickly.
rounds.nextRoundSuggestion: Don't repeat the same mistake on defense this round: close the A or B entry with a smoke, save the molly for the plant or post-plant, and hold an off-angle on the edge to wait out a long-sightline player like Chamber.

rounds.deathAnalysis: Late in this round on defense, time was on your side, but you took an early or unnecessary fight and died — your team was still alive, so you could have waited and forced a retake or a rotation.
enemyAnalysis: The enemy roster has Chamber; he held the long sightlines and waited for you.
With a numbers advantage on defense, split the corners with your team instead of opening up alone; if one player peeks, the other should be ready to trade.
rounds.nextRoundSuggestion: This round you could have given up the site and played for time; next round as Brimstone, close the most dangerous line with one smoke and save the molly for post-plant so your team keeps the edge on the retake.

rounds.deathAnalysis: This round you died taking an unnecessary risk on defense with your ult ready — instead of opening a solo fight with the ult in hand, you should have used it to take space and push the enemy back.
enemyAnalysis: The enemy roster has Chamber; you're facing an agent who locks down long sightlines and sharp angles.
Next round, use Brimstone's ult for pressure, not just defensively: break the angle Chamber is holding with the ult and push together with your team.
rounds.nextRoundSuggestion: On defense, don't take a solo risk like this round again.

rounds.deathAnalysis: Late in the post-plant you were left in the open and died as Brimstone without falling back — next time hold the post-plant from cover at the edge of the site, not out in the open.
enemyAnalysis: The enemy roster has Chamber; he can hold long sightlines and wait for you on a single angle.
You're playing Brimstone: instead of waiting on the edge alone without a smoke, cover the area around the spike with a molly or smoke and shift your position.
rounds.nextRoundSuggestion: On defense, don't wait in the open during the post-plant like this round; save the molly to delay the defuse, close one line with a smoke, then set up a crossfire from different cover.

rounds.deathAnalysis: The enemies squeezed the site toward the end of the round and used the clock; their tempo pressure forced you out of your defensive spot and you lost the timing on your fall-back or smoke — you're Brimstone, so don't stand in front of that window waiting without a smoke or your ult.
enemyAnalysis: An enemy trio finished the attack at high tempo and closed off the post-plant window.
To break it, one player should save a smoke for the retake or fall-back while another sets up a crossfire to control the area around the spike.
rounds.nextRoundSuggestion: On defense, fall back a step and save your smoke for the start of their entry.

rounds.deathAnalysis: You died in B Lobby with your ult ready; sitting on your ult left you with no impact after their entry — as Brimstone, use your ult for defensive pressure or fire it as you retreat.
enemyAnalysis: The enemy roster has Chamber and Neon; be ready for long-sightline and fast-entry combos.
Don't wait in B Lobby alone or without using utility; close the area with a smoke or molly together with your team, then hold.
rounds.nextRoundSuggestion: Don't hold B Lobby alone this defensive round; close the entry line with a smoke, save the molly for post-plant or to delay the defuse, and use your ult to pressure the area.

rounds.deathAnalysis: You stood in the open at B Main; on attack in a pistol round, dying to an early or late fight like this turns into an economic disadvantage — don't wait on that line with a wide angle without closing the B Main entry with a molly or smoke.
enemyAnalysis: Their roster has Chamber; he holds the long line and creates one-shot opportunities from that angle.
Close the B Main entry with a smoke or molly, bring a teammate with you and go in together so you're not the lone target.
rounds.nextRoundSuggestion: As Brimstone, close the B Main entry with a smoke and save the molly to delay the defuse after the plant — you'll be pushing in with your team, so don't wait alone on a wide angle.
